name: Crosshair-TS-TW
title: Crosshair Cursor
description: Two hairline white guides follow the mouse across a dark editorial panel, and they shudder with a noise glitch whenever the pointer touches a link.
use: An editorial or portfolio page wants a precise aiming reticle instead of a normal pointer.
avoid: It needs a mouse to appear, and the page must hide the real cursor or the two will overlap.
a11y: The guides only exist for a mouse; they vanish for keyboard users and there is no reduced-motion handling. (keyboard: n-a, labels: n-a, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: A near-black panel with a small letterspaced kicker, a heavy white headline, a line of grey copy and two underlined links. A one-pixel white horizontal and vertical line intersect where the pointer is, spanning the panel.
behaves: The two guide lines trail the pointer with a slight lag and fade in once the mouse enters. Hovering either link shakes both lines with a turbulence filter for half a second, then lets them settle.
customise: Line colour and the container to track are props; the glitch filter, the 0.15 follow lag and the line thickness are fixed in the source.
weight: light: Two one-pixel divs moved each frame, with a short SVG turbulence glitch on hover.
demo: Kicker "Field notes, vol. 04", headline "Aim small, miss small.", two links.
issues: The crosshair does nothing for keyboard users and hides when the pointer leaves the container.
If the page does not hide the native cursor, both pointers show at once.
polishWhy: Sharp editorial composition and a restrained glitch; the guides can cross the headline awkwardly.
